name: Potato Leaf (Healthy and Late Blight)
description:
The potato crop is found at fourth a major crop in the world, after rice, wheat, and maize. Nonetheless, in Ethiopia, the yield per unit area of potatoes is very low compared to other countries. There are a plethora of reasons, and one of them is the disease. The major disease, which affects the major potato production area is Late Blight, according to researchers the disease caused 100% crop loss on the unimproved local cultivar and 67.1% on a susceptible variety.

Not to take early Late Blight disease management would destroy the whole farm within a few days. For decades many researchers have experimented on plant disease detection and classification using computer vision via different approaches and algorithms. Many researchers used traditional machine learning algorithms which require a handcrafted feature extraction to detect a given image. Besides, the data collected were under a laboratory setup which makes it less reliable while testing in real cultivation farms captured images of the potato.

Heterogeneous image datasets were collected from (Holeta, Ethiopia) potato farm with the help of two plant pathologists. The dataset is correctly labeled with two classes as ‘Healthy’ and ‘Late Blight’, and the image has a variety meaning some of the images are captured with less noisy background images and others with a highly noisy environment. Under the ‘Late Blight’ class 63 images were collected and under the ‘Healthy’ class 363 images were collected. Finally, the prepared dataset could be used for different research that aimed at plant disease detection and classification.

method: The dataset was captured in a real potato farm in an uncontrolled environment. A high-resolution digital camera and smartphone were used. The potato farm is located in Holeta, Ethiopia. Dataset preparation is challenging. This dataset could help researchers in the field of computer vision.
